original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

scope_change_reason: Choose the selected source-binding preflight as the measured stage. Preserve live checker bytes because two registered audits pin them; provide an opt-in prototype, not production adoption.
actual_scope: Reuse canonical inventory paths within one selected-record check, preserving all source hashes and proof-membership checks under the retained stable-filesystem scope. Cover both manifest formats, the full current selected inventory, inherited regressions and fresh-call mutation controls.
bottleneck_link: Reduce repeated preflight verification work without caching successful checks or changing mathematical coverage. This saves only about 0.06-0.08 seconds per selected preflight on the measured host.
stop_rule: One measured preflight optimization; abandon if equivalence fails or alternating same-fixture timings show no improvement. No wider verifier rewrite or supplier work.
evidence: verify.py: 29 behavioral groups per engine and explicit optimized-CLI refusal; BENCHMARK.json and BENCHMARK-python312.json: nine fresh-process alternating pairs each, every call rehashes the full source inventory.

entry_overlap.limits: Titles/bodies/replies and top-level local notes, not arbitrary diffs or code. No match is not proof of novelty.
